title: Abu Hurayrah
hook: named for his little cat, he stayed close and carried the Prophet's words

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ibn Abbas, the young cousin the Prophet prayed for. Your line was: understanding prayed for. Which verse did you sit with, and what did it open? Today a new stretch of the road begins: later companions and their stories. Day eight hundred thirty-seven.

Father of the little cat. That is what the name means, and he explained it himself. As a boy he looked after his family's flock, and he had a small cat with him. At night he set it in a tree; by day he took it along and played with it. So people started calling him by it. Not by his father's name. By the cat. The report is kept by Tirmidhi. The nickname stuck, and it is the name heard whenever a hadith begins with him. Today: Abu Hurayrah, the companion named for a kitten.
screen: `A BOY, A FLOCK, A SMALL CAT.` → `THEY NAMED HIM FOR THE CAT.` → `ABU HURAYRAH.`

segments.voice: Abu Hurayrah had little to live on, and he made a choice about how to spend his days near the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. In Sahih al-Bukhari he answers people who complained that he narrated so much. The emigrants from Mecca, he says, were busy in the markets. The helpers of Medina were busy with their farms and property. He stayed close to the Prophet, content with enough food to keep him going, and so he was there when others were not, and remembered what others missed. In another report he says that once the Prophet told him to spread out his cloak while he spoke, then gather it to his chest, and after that he did not forget. And Bukhari records his own count of himself: none of the companions narrated more than he did, he said, except Abdullah ibn Amr, because Abdullah used to write things down, and he did not. So here is the picture. A man with no trade and no farm, often hungry, who decided that listening was his work. Now put the kitten back in the picture. Among the hadith that reach us through Abu Hurayrah is a story about a man who found a dog panting with thirst, climbed down a well, filled his shoe with water, and gave it a drink. God thanked him, the hadith says, and forgave him. The companions asked whether there is reward even for animals. The answer: in every living creature there is reward. A boy who kept a little cat with him grew into the man who carried that saying.
screen: `LITTLE TO LIVE ON.` · `OTHERS TRADED; HE LISTENED.` · `SPREAD YOUR CLOAK.` · `A DOG, A WELL, A SHOE OF WATER.` · then, large: `FATHER OF THE KITTEN.`

segments.voice: The practice: be kind to a cat. Or a dog, a bird, whatever creature shares your street. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one animal you will pass today. The neighbor's cat on the wall. A bird at the window. Something thirsty on a hot pavement. Breathe in, and see it clearly. Breathe out, and decide one small kindness: fresh water in a bowl, a slower step so you don't startle it, a gentle hand if it wants one. If you pray, you can say bismillah as you set the water down. The bell holds the time.
Abu Hurayrah. A nickname from a little cat, given to a poor companion who stayed close and listened, and through whom the Prophet's sayings still reach us. Today's word.
Your line: father of the kitten. Today, put out water for one creature, or slow down for one, and let a small mercy be part of your name. Day eight hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims hear Abu Hurayrah's name at the start of hadith, often followed by 'may God be pleased with him'; some Muslims also take his reports about mercy to animals as a reason to feed and water strays.

myth: Abu Hurayrah was his birth name
it's a nickname. he said people called him that because of the little cat he kept with him.
he said others were busy in markets and farms while he stayed close
that's his answer, in Bukhari, to people who said he narrated too much.
he said he narrated more than every other companion, with no exception
he named one exception: Abdullah ibn Amr, who wrote things down.

fork.setup: you are in Medina, poor, with no trade. the others go to the market or their fields. what do you do with your days?
options: find work in the market like everyone else.
stay close to the Prophet and listen.
fork.reveal: he stayed close, with just enough to eat, and so he was present when others were not. that is his own account, in Bukhari.

original.note: Arabic: 'father of the little cat'; hurayrah is a small form of the word for cat.

trapdoor: what you thought: a cute nickname, nothing more.
what it means: a poor companion who chose to stay near the Prophet and listen, so that he remembered what others missed.
what a scholar hears: in Bukhari he names Abdullah ibn Amr as narrating more, because Abdullah wrote things down and he did not.
